newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-RUSSIA CREATES COMMISSION TO TACKLE MATCH-FIXING.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RUSSIA CREATES COMMISSION TO TACKLE MATCH-FIXING.

text.p: Russian soccer authorities have set up a special commission to deal with match-fixing and corruption, a top official said on Monday.

Anatoly Gorokhovsky, head of the Russian Football Union's disciplinary committee, said a decision had been taken at the weekend to set up the commission after decades of rumours of bribery and corruption in Russian soccer.

Despite the rumours, succesful investigations or punishments over the years have been rare. But Russia's new criminal code formally describes bribery of players and organisers of sports competitions as a crime.

"For the first time the new criminal code which took effect on January 1 sets out punishments for bribery and fixed matches. The commission will watch games, videotape them and gather other material to open a criminal case," Gorokhovsky told Reuters by telephone.
"For decades there was public and private talk of fixed matches and bribery of referees and players. The time has come to fight the dirty people who have penetrated our sport."
Gorokhovsky made no mention of any alleged match-fixing or other crimes already under investigation.
